description: QueryDoc AI retrieval evaluation set. Questions were written during development by reading the extracted text of four public-domain NIST publications. Each answerable question lists one or more evidence spans copied verbatim from the document; a retrieved chunk is relevant when it covers at least 50% of the characters of any evidence span (see src/querydoc/evaluation/relevance.py). Labels were authored with AI assistance and have not been independently reviewed by a second human annotator.
split_rule: Questions with odd numeric ids are 'dev' (used for tuning); even ids are 'test' (held out, reported).

questions.question: What is the minimum length for a password that the user picks themselves?
evidence: Verifiers SHALL require subscriber-chosen memorized secrets to be at least 8 characters
Memorized secrets SHALL be at least 8 characters in length if chosen by the subscriber

questions.question: Up to what length should verifiers allow user-chosen passwords so passphrases are possible?
evidence: SHOULD permit subscriber-chosen memorized secrets at least 64 characters

questions.question: Should a verifier force users to mix uppercase, digits and symbols in their passwords?
evidence: Verifiers SHOULD NOT impose other composition rules

questions.question: Is it recommended to make users change their passwords on a regular schedule?
evidence: SHOULD NOT require memorized secrets to be changed arbitrarily

questions.question: At assurance level 2, how often must a subscriber authenticate again even if they stay active?
evidence: At AAL2, authentication of the subscriber SHALL be repeated at least once per 12 hours

questions.question: At AAL3, how long can a session sit idle before the user has to reauthenticate?
evidence: 15 minutes or longer. Reauthentication SHALL use both authentication factors

questions.question: By default, what is the cap on consecutive failed sign-in attempts for one account?
evidence: limit consecutive failed authentication attempts on a single account to no more than 100

questions.question: How long does the salt need to be when password hashes are stored?
evidence: The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length

questions.question: What minimum entropy is required for look-up secret codes?
evidence: Look-up secrets SHALL have at least 20 bits of entropy

questions.question: What is the time limit for completing an out-of-band authentication?
evidence: SHALL be considered invalid if not completed within 10 minutes

questions.question: What false match rate does a biometric system have to meet?
evidence: FMR [ISO/IEC 2382-37] of 1 in 1000 or better

questions.question: Without presentation attack detection, how many failed biometric tries in a row are permitted?
evidence: allow no more than 5 consecutive failed authentication attempts

questions.question: How much entropy must the secrets used for session binding contain?
evidence: and contain at least 64 bits of entropy

questions.question: For how long is a confirmation code that is mailed to a postal address valid?
evidence: SHALL be valid for a maximum of 7 days

questions.question: May email or VoIP be used as an out-of-band authenticator channel?
evidence: SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication

questions.question: Can a verifier let users save a password reminder that anyone can see before logging in?
evidence: Memorized secret verifiers SHALL NOT permit the subscriber to store a "hint"

questions.question: Should users be able to paste their password into the login field?
evidence: Verifiers SHOULD permit claimants to use "paste" functionality

questions.question: What must happen if a newly chosen password appears on a list of breached values?
evidence: SHALL advise the subscriber that they need to select a different secret

questions.question: How frequently should subscribers at AAL1 be reauthenticated?
evidence: At AAL1, reauthentication of the subscriber SHOULD be repeated at least once per 30 days

questions.question: How does an incident precursor differ from an indicator?
evidence: A precursor is a sign that an incident may occur in the future
An indicator is a sign that an incident may have occurred or may be occurring now

questions.question: Which incident response team structure fits a small organization with little geographic spread?
evidence: A single incident response team handles incidents throughout the organization
This model is effective for small organizations

questions.question: Which team model suits large organizations with computing resources in distant locations?
evidence: The organization has multiple incident response teams, each responsible for a particular logical or physical segment

questions.question: What is a coordinating incident response team?
evidence: An incident response team provides advice to other teams without having authority over those teams
This model can be thought of as a CSIRT for CSIRTs

questions.question: Which attack vector describes malware that spreads from an infected USB stick?
evidence: An attack executed from removable media or a peripheral device

questions.question: What kind of attack is classified as attrition?
evidence: An attack that employs brute force methods to compromise, degrade, or destroy systems

questions.question: Why is it important to keep the clocks of all hosts in sync?
evidence: Event correlation will be more complicated if the devices reporting events have inconsistent clock settings

questions.question: How soon after an incident ends should the lessons learned meeting take place?
evidence: should be held within several days of the end of the incident

questions.question: Is it acceptable to review more than one incident in the same post-incident meeting?
evidence: Multiple incidents can be covered in a single lessons learned meeting

questions.question: What does a medium functional impact rating mean for an incident?
evidence: Organization has lost the ability to provide a critical service to a subset of system users

questions.question: Which recoverability category applies when sensitive data has been exfiltrated and published?
evidence: Recovery from the incident is not possible

questions.question: What does the supplemented recoverability effort category mean?
evidence: Time to recovery is predictable with additional resources

questions.question: For how long do most organizations keep evidence after an incident?
evidence: organizations choose to retain all evidence for months or years after the incident ends

questions.question: If the attacker might be prosecuted, how long should incident evidence be kept?
evidence: evidence may need to be retained until all legal actions have been completed

questions.question: Why should incident handlers study how networks and systems normally behave?
evidence: understand what their normal behavior is so that abnormal behavior can be

questions.question: What are the four functions in the core of the AI risk management framework?
evidence: These functions - GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE

questions.question: Which characteristics make an AI system trustworthy according to the framework?
evidence: systems include: valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent

questions.question: Does the AI RMF tell organizations what level of risk they should accept?
evidence: it does not prescribe risk tolerance

questions.question: How does the framework define risk tolerance?
evidence: readiness to bear the risk in order to achieve its objectives

questions.question: What is residual risk?
evidence: defined as risk remaining after risk treatment

questions.question: What is the difference between explainability and interpretability of an AI system?
evidence: Explainability refers to a representation of the mechanisms underlying AI systems' operation
interpretability refers to the meaning of AI systems' output

questions.question: If harmful bias has been mitigated, is the AI system automatically fair?
evidence: Systems in which harmful biases are mitigated are not necessarily fair

questions.question: What are the three major categories of AI bias identified by NIST?
evidence: three major categories of AI bias to be considered and managed: systemic, computational

questions.question: After putting governance outcomes in place, which function do most users begin with?
evidence: most users of the AI RMF would start with the MAP function

questions.question: Which AI RMF function is cross-cutting across the whole risk management process?
evidence: GOVERN is a cross-cutting function that is infused throughout AI risk management

questions.question: Which subcategory requires an inventory of AI systems?
evidence: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems

questions.question: What are temporal profiles in the AI RMF?
evidence: AI RMF temporal profiles are descriptions of either the current state or the desired, target

questions.question: What do cross-sectoral AI RMF profiles address?
evidence: AI RMF cross-sectoral profiles cover risks of models or applications that can be used across

questions.question: Why are AI systems called socio-technical?
evidence: AI systems are inherently socio-technical in nature

questions.question: How many steps make up the Risk Management Framework?
evidence: There are seven steps in the RMF

questions.question: What does reciprocity mean between organizations?
evidence: Reciprocity is an agreement between organizations to accept one another's security assessment results

questions.question: What are the possible outputs of the authorization decision task?
evidence: Authorization to operate, authorization to use, common control authorization; denial

questions.question: Who sets the date when a system's authorization expires?
evidence: The authorization termination date is established by the authorizing official

questions.question: Under what condition can an organization drop the authorization termination date?
evidence: Organizations may eliminate the authorization termination date if the system is operating under an ongoing authorization

questions.question: What is a hybrid control?
evidence: In such cases, the control is considered a hybrid control

questions.question: What results from applying the high-water mark concept to categorized systems?
evidence: results in systems designated as low impact, moderate impact, or high impact

questions.question: What documents go into the package submitted to the authorizing official?
evidence: Authorization package (with an executive summary)
Security and privacy plans; security and privacy assessment reports; plan of action and milestones

questions.question: What happens in task C-3 of the Categorize step?
evidence: Review and approve the security categorization results and decision

questions.question: What is done in task S-2 of the Select step?
evidence: Tailor the controls selected for the system and the environment of operation

questions.question: What is the first task in the Assess step?
evidence: Select the appropriate assessor or assessment team

questions.question: Besides impact of loss, which risk factors are considered during risk assessment?
evidence: the other three factors being threats, vulnerabilities, and likelihood of occurrence

questions.question: What does task M-1 of the Monitor step require?
evidence: Monitor the information system and its environment of operation for changes

questions.question: What is task I-2 in the Implement step?
evidence: Document changes to planned control implementations

questions.question: At which levels of the risk management hierarchy can common controls be allocated?
evidence: common controls may be allocated at the organization, mission/business process, or information system level
